name: First Things First
pages: If you are reading this Handbook, you are either shipwrecked, or will become so some Day. In such Circumstance, preserving one's Life is paramount.$(br)    First Priority is a hasty Survey of the Island upon whose Shore the Sea has disgorged you, seeking improvised Shelter and such Sustenance as the Land may offer.$(br)    The Castaway begins armed only with their own Ingenuity, but this Condition is temporary. Tools more able than Hands are required forthwith.

pages.title: Tools from the Sea
pages.text: Hard Stone is abundant and suitable for crafting Tools, but offers a Paradox: How may one work Stone without possessing Stone? Fortune supplies several Options.$(br)    Beaches and Shores are littered with Sea-Shells strong enough to break Stone, providing Material for one's first Implements.

pages.title: A Dubious Alternative
pages.text: If one's Luck is so poor that no Shells may be found, the unfortunate may scrounge in the Gravel for Flints large enough to serve, though such a Tool is crude, fragile, and ultimately to be cast aside.

pages.title: A Boon Companion
pages.text: Once Implements for working Stone and Wood are secured, a wise Castaway surveys for the Glint of Copper amid the dull Rocks. The merest Lump provides ample Stuff to craft a Knife-Blade, and a Knife is a versatile Assistant, capable of cutting Grasses into Straw, butchering Animals, and hacking a Path through dense Foliage.

pages.title: Victuals
pages.text: Rations are the next Priority, for an empty Belly kills more surely than any Predator, and Hunger grows apace, whether one labors or stands idle.$(br)    Some Islands may offer Fruits or other Greenery, but Chance may provide only Fish or Flesh as Food. A trusty Knife or Spear should suffice to bring down small Game.

pages: In the Waters, the desperate may seize Fish by Hand, but even the meanest of Tools will give better Result. The many scuttling Denizens of the Shore-Line provide succulent Tidbits for the unsqueamish.$(br)    Hunger may provoke one to feed greedily upon the first raw Meat obtained, but let Reason prevail - cook all Foods for superior Sustenance and Preservation.$(br)    If the Island be too miserly to provide sufficient Copper for Pots and Pans, a Camp-fire will suffice.

Once one's Belly and Ration-Bag have been provided for, seek a Shelter for the Night. The meanest of Accommodations will suffice - a small Chamber dug into a Hillside, a crude Hut of Wood, or even the Limbs of a Tree.$(br)    If Wool cannot be found for Bedding, an improvised Bedroll can be made from Canvas, though such is not reusable.$(br)    Light the Surroundings well with Camp-fires or Torches to keep Creatures at bay, and if Sleep will not come, do such Work as one can until Morning.
